annotations.description: Casting Slickshot Show-Off in the precombat main phase is suboptimal when holding multiple combat tricks (Dreadmaw's Ire, Full Bore, Might of the Meek, Bulk Up). The opponent has only 1 Island untapped (no counterspell mana), so there's minimal risk of it being countered. However, playing it pre-combat reveals information unnecessarily and means the opponent knows about it before declaring blockers. More importantly, Slickshot Show-Off has Plot for {1}{R} - plotting it would let you deploy it for free on a later turn while keeping mana open for combat tricks. With only 2 Mountains available, casting Show-Off uses all mana and prevents casting any combat tricks this turn. Plotting it would also use all mana but set up a much more explosive future turn where you can cast Show-Off for free and chain multiple pump spells.

annotations.betterLine: Plot Slickshot Show-Off for {1}{R} to set up a future explosive turn where you can cast it for free and chain pump spells with full mana available. annotations.description: Casting Bulk Up (a combat trick that doubles power) during precombat main phase is wasteful in multiple ways. First, it tips off the opponent before blocks are declared. Second and more critically, with Leyline of Resonance in hand (which copies instants/sorceries targeting a single creature you control), GLM47 should have played Leyline of Resonance first to get double value from combat tricks. Additionally, casting combat tricks before combat means the opponent sees the pump and can plan accordingly. With only 1 Island on the opponent's board, there's minimal counterplay risk, but the sequencing is still wrong. The Leyline of Resonance would double every subsequent combat trick (Bulk Up, Full Bore, Dreadmaw's Ire, Might of the Meek), providing enormous value over the game.

annotations.description: GLM47 attacked with only Stadium Headliner instead of all creatures. The opponent has only 1 untapped Island and no creatures to block.
